title: [D1 Ingest] Normalizer core with identity stamping from configuration
summary: `helena.normalizer` now produces a `NormalizedEvent` — an `identity` block (tenant, sensor, schema version, event id, raw-record reference) beside an `observation` block that is still the record exactly as supplied. `Normalizer.from_settings(settings)` stamps the identity from deployment configuration only, refuses to exist without a non-blank tenant and sensor, and derives a deterministic event id as a sha256 over tenant, sensor, capture digest and record offset, so replaying a capture reproduces every id.
assumption_validated: That identity can be assigned entirely outside the record without the record being able to influence it, and that an event id can be deterministic without a clock, a counter or a store. Both hold and are demonstrated: normalizing the same record under two configurations yields two identities and two ids while the observation compares equal; normalizing all 62 records of data/ingest/flow-sample.jsonl twice yields events that compare equal field for field, ids included. A negative result worth recording: the event id CANNOT be derived from the capture reference and offset alone as the PRD step described — see invariant_conflicts.
makes_buildable: Task 8 (adapter protocol) has the output type an adapter must produce — `NormalizedEvent` — and the stamping call it wraps, so a second adapter can be added without touching the event contract. Task 9 (quarantine) has the exact reference a quarantine row needs (`RawRecordReference`: capture sha256 + zero-based offset) already modelled, and the two typed failures to route: `ValidationError` from the contract and `CaptureError` from an offset that addresses no record. Task 10 (broker wiring) has `normalize_capture` as the one path from a capture to events, so the consumer and the replay driver cannot become two implementations, and `identity.raw_record.record_offset` reconciles against `Capture.record_count`. Task 12 (flatten views) has the four identity columns it must carry into every flatten row, and `EVENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` for the table that first stores an event — that is where its second, SQL copy and the equality test belong.

verification.detail: 307 passed in 13.2 s (was 282; 25 new tests). `uv lock --check` clean, compileall clean. The suite includes the engine-backed migration and version tests, which ran rather than skipped. No new SQL in this task — nothing stores a normalized event yet. Four mutation checks were run against the new tests before believing them, each restored afterwards: (1) replacing the length-prefixed event-id encoding with a plain delimiter join fails the ambiguity test; (2) removing tenant and sensor from the digest fails the two-configurations test; (3) disabling the blank-identity refusal fails the refusal test; (4) adding os.urandom to the digest fails the replay-determinism test. Relaxing the `Identifier` pattern to plain `str` fails the three blank-tenant cases.

invariant_conflicts.step: Generate a deterministic event id from capture reference plus record offset so replay reproduces ids
invariant_conflicts.detail: Implemented as capture reference plus record offset PLUS tenant and sensor. Capture-plus-offset alone means two deployments ingesting the same capture file mint identical event ids in the single store, and task 4 measured that a RisingWave INSERT onto an existing primary key is an UPSERT that overwrites the row and raises nothing — so the narrower derivation is a silent cross-tenant overwrite that looks like it is working, which is the exact failure `concept/instruction.md` §6 and `concept/07-principles.md` name for a defaulted tenant. The step's replay property is unaffected: tenant and sensor come from configuration and do not change on a replay. The cost, stated in the code and in ADR-0011 rather than hidden: an id is reproducible only under the identity that made it, so re-ingesting a capture under a renamed tenant produces new ids.
invariant_conflicts.resolution: Strengthened rather than skipped; recorded in docs/decisions/0011 and pinned by tests.

invariant_conflicts.step: Implement the normalized event model with an identity block (… schema version …)
invariant_conflicts.detail: Not a conflict between documents, but a name collision between two contracts that both call a field `schema_version`. `EVENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` (helena.normalizer) versions the shape of an ingested event; `VersionSet.schema_version` (helena.versions) versions the agent output schema a stored assessment is replayed against. `concept/03-architecture.md` uses the phrase for the first and `concept/07-principles.md` for the second. Nothing joins them today; a test pins the collision so the increment where an event row first cites a version set finds it already known rather than discovering it in a column name.

deferred: Any SQL. Nothing stores a normalized event until task 10 wires the broker and the engine, so there is no table, no view and no second copy of EVENT_SCHEMA_VERSION to assert equal. Inventing the table here would be writing task 10's and task 12's contract ahead of them; the increment that creates it adds the SQL copy and the equality test with it.

Counting the new failure paths. `ValidationError` (invalid record), `CaptureError` (an offset that addresses no record) and `ConfigurationError` (a blank identity) are each typed and each fails loud, but none is stored or counted — quarantine rows and the ingest counters are tasks 9 and 10, which are what will have somewhere to put them. Nothing is dropped silently in the meantime: normalize raises and the caller stops.

Any use of `helena.observability`. Nothing here logs. The normalizer has an identity now, so a logger is finally constructible from it, but a log line with no consumer and no ingest run to attribute it to would be structure ahead of the increment.

An ingestion timestamp on the event, deliberately and permanently as far as this contract goes: a wall-clock field would make every replay differ from the run it replays. Arrival time is a property of a run and belongs to whatever records runs.

A per-record tenant argument, and any notion of more than one sensor per normalizer. `concept/06-technology.md` and `concept/08-open-questions.md` record that deployment-configured identity does not scale to multiple sensors sharing one normalizer; the trigger is a second sensor, and the shape when it arrives is a second `Normalizer`, not an argument a caller can get wrong per record.
lessons: task 07: Pydantic 2.13 `strict=True` still ACCEPTS a plain dict for a nested model field (measured: `EventIdentity(..., raw_record={'capture_sha256': ..., 'record_offset': 0})` validates). Strict mode constrains scalar coercion, not model construction from a mapping. Worth knowing before writing a test that relies on a dict being rejected — it will pass for the wrong reason.

task 07: A tenant is an operator-supplied string, so any delimiter can occur inside one. Joining identity parts with a separator before hashing makes `tenant='a'/sensor='b:c'` and `tenant='a:b'/sensor='c'` collide into one id for two tenants. The event id length-prefixes each part (`<utf8 len>:<bytes>`) and a test asserts the two differ.

task 07: The two halves of 'the record cannot influence the tenant' need two different tests, because `extra="forbid"` only covers the first. A record carrying a tenant FIELD is refused outright (nothing to stamp); a record whose VALUES name a tenant — a DNS name, a URI, the producer's own `id` — is perfectly valid input, and the only demonstration that it cannot reach the identity is normalizing it under a differently-configured Normalizer and asserting the stamped tenant character for character.

task 07: `tests/test_normalizer.py::_contract_models()` walks outward from `FlowRecord` only, which is what keeps `test_the_contract_reaches_every_nested_model` at 15 models now that `NormalizedEvent` exists. Walking from `NormalizedEvent` instead would sweep the identity block into the absence tests and fail every one of them — the identity block is precisely where those fields are supposed to be.

task 07: Identity is refused rather than defaulted at three places, and all three are needed: `Settings.load` (unset/blank variable at startup), `Normalizer.__post_init__` (an `IngestionIdentity` assembled some other way — a test, or a caller that thought it had one), and the `EventIdentity` field pattern (` acme` and `acme` must not become two tenants that look like one). `helena.observability._required` is a fourth instance of the same rule for the same reason.

task 07: With no linter in the project (ADR-0003), the convention that holds is 88 columns; `awk 'length>88'` over the changed files is the cheap check. Three pre-existing over-length lines in tests/test_normalizer.py were left alone.
failed_approaches: task 07: Deriving the event id from the capture reference and the record offset alone, as the PRD step describes, was written and then widened before reporting — see invariant_conflicts. It is deterministic and it replays correctly, and it is still wrong: it makes two tenants' ids collide in the one store, where an INSERT onto an existing key silently upserts. Do not narrow it back.

task 07: Putting `EVENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` into the event-id digest was considered and rejected before it was written. It versions the shape of the event, not which record it is, so mixing it in would change every id the first time the shape changed and the replay guarantee would hold only until the next version bump.

task 07: Adding an `ingested_at` field to the event was considered and rejected for the same family of reasons — it would make 'a capture replayed twice produces identical rows' (task 11's test) impossible to state, and the fix would then be to exclude the field from the comparison, which is the same thing as not having it.
next_session_should_know: Produce events through `Normalizer.from_settings(settings)` and nothing else — `normalize(capture, offset, line)` for one record, `normalize_capture(capture)` for a whole capture in file order, and do not write a second stamping path, because replay must exercise the same one as live ingestion. Five things that will bite otherwise. (1) `normalize` does NOT catch anything: an invalid record raises `ValidationError`, an offset outside the capture raises `CaptureError`, and a blank identity raises `ConfigurationError` at construction. Task 9's quarantine is what turns the first two into typed rows; until then a bad record kills the caller, which is deliberate. (2) The event id is a sha256 over tenant, sensor, capture digest and offset — WIDER than the PRD step said, because capture-plus-offset alone collides across tenants in a store where INSERT upserts silently (docs/decisions/0011). It is reproducible only under the identity that made it. (3) `EVENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` lives in `helena.normalizer` and has ONE home today; the increment that creates the first table holding a normalized event must add the SQL copy and the test asserting the two equal, the way `helena.versions.AGGREGATION_VERSION` and migration 0002 already do. Note that it is a different dimension from `VersionSet.schema_version` (the agent output schema) despite the identical field name — a row carrying both needs two column names. (4) The identity block is `tenant`, `sensor`, `schema_version`, `event_id`, `raw_record{capture_sha256, record_offset}`; those are the columns task 12 must carry into every flatten row, and `concept/03-architecture.md` is explicit that stamping them is a seam, not isolation enforcement — do not claim more. (5) There is still no engine table, no logging and no counter on this path, and capture identity remains provisional under live ingestion (ADR-0010), so every event id derived from an open file is provisional too. Still open and untouched: the concept/05 vs data/netify tension, bin/README.md's dangling reference to scripts/build-binaries.sh, and there is still no git repository, so nothing here was committed.
